decision.summary: The rotten-egg smell from the boiler is a possible gas leak, so it is an emergency despite the tenant calling it "not urgent". I opened emergency job JOB-101, told the tenant to leave and call 0800 111 999, assigned HeatRight Ltd for an out-of-hours visit, notified the landlord, and escalated P1 as ESC-105 for a human to confirm attendance tonight.

answers.question: 1. What severity is this and why, given the tenant says it is "not urgent"?
answers.answer: Emergency. A rotten-egg smell from a gas boiler is the standard sign of a gas leak (mercaptan odourant). The tenant's "not urgent" wording does not lower the risk, and an 82-year-old guest is in the flat.

answers.question: 2. What exactly do you tell the tenant right now, and in what order?
answers.answer: First: leave the flat with everyone, open windows if safe, and avoid switches, cooker, flames and electrical devices. Second: once outside, call 0800 111 999 even if the smell has gone. Third: call 999 if anyone feels unwell. Fourth: do not return until the engineer says it is safe. Last: an engineer is being arranged and we will message when a visit time is confirmed. Sent as MSG-102 (ledger A2).

answers.question: 3. Which actions do you take tonight (job, contractor, escalation, landlord)?
answers.answer: Created emergency gas job JOB-101 (A1). Assigned HeatRight Ltd (C-11, Gas Safe 550123) for an out-of-hours visit (A3) and texted them (A5). Emailed landlord Ben Hartley that make-safe does not need his approval but anything over £300 inc VAT does (A4). Escalated P1 as ESC-105 (A6) for a human to confirm attendance and check the tenant has left.

args.body:
Hi Amelia, thanks for telling us. A rotten-egg smell from the boiler can mean a gas leak, so please treat this as an emergency, even though it's late.

Please do this now:
1. Open the windows and leave the flat, taking everyone with you, including your flatmate's mum.
2. Don't use any light switches, the cooker, flames, or electrical devices inside the flat.
3. Once you're outside, call the National Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999. Do this even if the smell has gone.
4. Don't go back in until the gas engineer says it's safe.

If anyone feels unwell, dizzy or sick, call 999.

I'm arranging an emergency gas engineer now. We'll message you as soon as we have a confirmed visit time. Reply here if you have any questions.
